questions.question: You want to park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels so the car will roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail. Do this when parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Stop and stay stopped until the light changes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Come to a full stop, look for other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: If your tires feel like they are not touching the road, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear to slow down.
Pump the brakes hard and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal slowly.
questions.explanation: Release the gas pedal and do not use the brakes. Wait until your tires grip the road again before stopping or turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Get ready for traffic to merge into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready for traffic to merge into your lane.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic will merge into your lane from the right. Be ready to let them in safely.

questions.question: When dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should drive slowly and turn on your:
questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking downhill or uphill without a curb, turn them toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: This pennant-shaped yellow sign warns that you cannot pass other vehicles in this area.

questions.question: You reach a four-way stop at the same time as the driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to turn has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are what color?
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic laws they must follow. These signs are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green text or symbols.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not entered yet. You should:

options.text: Speed up to cross before the red light.
Slow down and drive through carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it quickly. If you have not entered, stop if you can do so safely.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice in a car with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Take your foot off the brakes and let the car stop on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and keep it pressed. The system will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines are used to:

options.text: Separate lanes moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A dashed or broken line means you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: How far ahead of your vehicle should you look?
questions.correctAnswerText: One city block
questions.explanation: Look at least one city block ahead. This helps you spot hazards early and avoid sudden stops or turns.

questions.question: When roads are wet and slippery after rain starts, you should:

options.text: Test your tire grip while going uphill.
Look closer to your vehicle instead of ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire traction. Drive slowly and avoid sharp turns or sudden stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: Having a driver license is a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must follow the rules to keep everyone safe. If you break traffic laws, your license can be taken away.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, check traffic by:

options.text: Using your rearview and side mirrors.
Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic clearly when entering a freeway.

questions.question: Large trucks are likely to lose speed when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to speed up than smaller vehicles. They lose speed going up long or steep hills. Give them extra space, especially on hills.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are to your left and parked vehicles are to your right. You should steer:

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: Steer down the middle between the oncoming cars and the parked cars.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: Finish crossing the intersection, then drive to the right and stop. Always yield to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: If your car's rear end skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: Take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This brings the front of the car in line with the rear.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians crossing any street, marked or unmarked. For safety, always give pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
Turn on your high beam headlights to better see the vehicles ahead of you.
Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly at night so you can stop within the lit area of your headlights. You cannot see as far ahead at night.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop, if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill. Slow down so you can stop if a vehicle is stalled ahead.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start to prepare to slow down.
Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: Use a sharp horn blast when a child or pedestrian is about to enter the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
More dangerous than not driving defensively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe strategies to prevent crashes. Adjust your driving for weather, how you feel, and what other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians are doing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Are traveling in the wrong direction.
Must treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign.
May not proceed until it changes to green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Stop completely at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction the arrow points, but first yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: Check your rearview mirrors:

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors frequently. This helps you know where vehicles are near you.

questions.question: If your car begins to skid out of control, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, do not use the brakes. Keep steering until the car is under control and moving safely.
